# Every finite Jordan paired quotient is generated by stabilizer-killed squares

Date: 2026-08-11

## 1. Outcome

The one-block calculation in
`FALSE_NONCOMMUTING_CONGRUENCE_BOCKSTEIN.md` extends exactly to every
finite collection of first-congruence Jordan blocks.  The resulting paired
Bockstein quotient has one dimension per block, but it has no cross-block
classes: it is generated by the individual square cycles

`[b_i|b_i]`.                                                `(FJ1)`

By `FALSE_NONCOMMUTING_BOCKSTEIN_STABILIZER_CANCELLATION.md`, every cycle
in `(FJ1)` is induced from a polynomial double-coset stabilizer.  Therefore
the entire paired quotient of every finite Jordan quotient disappears after
the stabilizer-homology relations are imposed.

This is a finite-quotient no-go theorem.  It does not prove that the full
Laurent intermediate group has zero marked paired quotient: a surviving
class would have to use deeper congruence information or derived exterior
data which does not factor through any of the finite first-order Jordan
quotients below.

## 2. The finite Jordan group

Let

`V_m=<a_1,b_1,...,a_m,b_m> ~= (C_2)^(2m)`,             `(FJ2)`

and let `t` act on `V_m` by

`t a_i t^(-1)=a_i`,
`t b_i t^(-1)=a_i b_i`.                               `(FJ3)`

Put

`Q_m=V_m semidirect <t>`.                              `(FJ4)`

Thus `Q_1` is the dihedral group `D_8` used in the preceding notes.  For
each `i` there is a split retraction

`q_i:Q_m->Q_1`                                        `(FJ5)`

which keeps `a_i,b_i,t` and kills `a_j,b_j` for `j!=i`.

Let `M_+=Z` be the trivial coefficient module and let `M_-=Z_chi`, where
`V_m` acts trivially and `t` acts by `-1`.  Reduction modulo two identifies
both modules with `F_2`.  Write

`beta_+:H_2(Q_m,F_2)->H_1(Q_m,M_+)`,
`beta_-:H_2(Q_m,F_2)->H_1(Q_m,M_-)`                  `(FJ6)`

for the two coefficient Bocksteins, and define the paired quotient

`P_m=H_2(Q_m,F_2)/(ker(beta_+)+ker(beta_-))`.          `(FJ7)`

## 3. Exact computation of the paired quotient

**Theorem 1.**  The square cycles

`s_i=[b_i|b_i]`, `1<=i<=m`,                           `(FJ8)`

descend to a basis of `P_m`.  In particular,

`P_m ~= (F_2)^m`.                                     `(FJ9)`

### Proof: independence

The cycle `s_i` is well defined because `b_i^2=1`.  Its two Bocksteins are

`beta_+(s_i)=[b_i]`, `beta_-(s_i)=[b_i]`.             `(FJ10)`

For `m=1`, Section 2 of
`FALSE_NONCOMMUTING_BOCKSTEIN_STABILIZER_CANCELLATION.md` proves

`P_1=F_2 [b|b]`.                                      `(FJ11)`

Suppose that

`sum_i epsilon_i s_i in ker(beta_+)+ker(beta_-)`.     `(FJ12)`

Apply the retraction `q_j`.  Naturality of both coefficient Bocksteins
sends the right-hand side of `(FJ12)` into the sum of the two one-block
kernels, while the left-hand side maps to

`epsilon_j [b|b]`.                                    `(FJ13)`

Equation `(FJ11)` forces `epsilon_j=0`.  Since this holds for every `j`,
the classes in `(FJ8)` are independent in `P_m`.

### Proof: the matching upper bound

We compute the twisted first homology.  Use the split extension

`1->V_m->Q_m->C_2->1`.                                `(FJ14)`

The total-degree-one terms of the Lyndon--Hochschild--Serre homology
spectral sequence with coefficients `M_-` are

`H_1(C_2,M_-)=0`,                                     `(FJ15)`

and

`H_0(C_2,H_1(V_m,M_-))`
` ~= V_m/(t-1)V_m`.                                   `(FJ16)`

The sign in the action on `M_-` disappears on the elementary two-group
`H_1(V_m,M_-)~=V_m`.  From `(FJ3)`,

`(t-1)b_i=a_i`, `(t-1)a_i=0`;                         `(FJ17)`

hence

`V_m/(t-1)V_m=<bar b_1,...,bar b_m> ~= (C_2)^m`.      `(FJ18)`

The transgression in total degree one vanishes because `(FJ14)` is split.
Therefore

`H_1(Q_m,M_-) ~= (C_2)^m`.                            `(FJ19)`

For any two linear maps `F,G` on a finite-dimensional vector space,

`dim(V/(ker F+ker G))<=rank(G)`.                       `(FJ20)`

Apply `(FJ20)` to `beta_+,beta_-`.  Equation `(FJ19)` gives

`dim_F2(P_m)<=rank(beta_-)<=m`.                        `(FJ21)`

The `m` independent square classes already constructed force equality in
`(FJ21)`, proving `(FJ9)`.  This completes the proof.

## 4. Polynomial stabilizers kill the whole finite quotient

Return to the Laurent setup

`R=Z[x_1^(+-1),...,x_d^(+-1)]`,
`R_+=Z[x_1,...,x_d]`,
`E=EL_r(R)`, `Gamma=EL_r(R_+)`, `r>=5`,
`B_2=<ker(E->EL_r(R/2R)),e_12(x_1^(-1))>`.            `(FJ22)`

Choose distinct Laurent monomials `f_1,...,f_m`.  The first-congruence
quotient on their independent adjoint Jordan blocks gives a quotient

`pi_m:B_2->Q_m`                                       `(FJ23)`

with

`a_i=pi_m(e_13(2f_i))`,
`b_i=pi_m(e_23(2x_1f_i))`,
`t=pi_m(e_12(x_1^(-1)))`.                             `(FJ24)`

For each `i`, the preceding stabilizer-cancellation note constructs a
double-coset representative `d_i in E` and a cycle

`U_i in Z_2(B_2 intersect d_i Gamma d_i^(-1),F_2)`    `(FJ25)`

such that

`(pi_m)_*[U_i]=[b_i|b_i]=s_i`.                        `(FJ26)`

Indeed, `U_i` is the sum of `[b_i|b_i]` and the explicit five-term bar
filling of the Steinberg commutator identity

`b_i^2=[e_24(2x_1f_i),e_43(2)]`.                      `(FJ27)`

Combining Theorem 1 with `(FJ26)` proves:

**Corollary 2.**  The map from polynomial double-coset stabilizer homology
onto the paired quotient is surjective:

`sum_d im H_2(B_2 intersect d Gamma d^(-1),F_2)`
` -> P_m`                                              `(FJ28)`

is onto after applying `pi_m`.  Equivalently, the further quotient

`H_2(Q_m,F_2) /`
` (ker(beta_+)+ker(beta_-)+<stabilizer images>)`       `(FJ29)`

is zero.

Thus no class whose simultaneous-Bockstein information factors completely
through a finite direct sum of the first-order noncommuting Jordan blocks
can couple to the Laurent radical relation module.

## 5. What remains

The FALSE search must now leave the finite first-congruence Jordan layer.
The remaining possibilities are narrower:

1. a higher `2`-power congruence class whose square filling cannot be
   conjugated into a polynomial stabilizer;
2. a genuinely infinite-support compatible class which is zero in every
   `P_m` but nonzero before taking the direct limit or completion;
3. a derived exterior-square or higher stabilizer-resolution class not
   represented by a base-row square cycle; or
4. a different prime/local system for which the twisted first-homology
   bound does not force the paired quotient to be generated by cyclic
   square classes.

The important point is that merely adding more independent first-order
Jordan blocks cannot help: Theorem 1 computes that entire finite sector,
and Corollary 2 kills it.
